title: The REX prefix
description:
Decode the REX prefix byte of x64 instructions.

```
48 -> REX.W (64-bit operand)
4C -> REX.W R (64-bit, reg field +8)
41 -> REX B (r/m or base field +8)
40 -> REX with no bits (gives access to sil, dil, spl, bpl)
90 -> not a REX prefix
```
hints: `(b & 0xF0) == 0x40` is a REX; W is `b & 8`, R `b & 4`, X `b & 2`, B `b & 1` (lesson 5.01).
The register names in order are rax, rcx, rdx, rbx, rsp, rbp, rsi, rdi, then r8 to r15.
requirements: A REX byte is `0x40` to `0x4F`; its low four bits are W, R, X and B.
Explain what each set bit does.
Show the register a ModRM field of 1 becomes with and without R (rcx vs r9).
stretch: Decode a VEX prefix (`C4`/`C5`) too. It is not covered in this course: look up its layout in the Intel Software Developer's Manual, volume 2, "VEX prefix".
